evidence: Lucr. 5.151 (Lewis & Short s.v. tactilis: “that may be touched”)
terms.comment: Our phrase: no reference work has a word for a touchscreen. Traupman’s quadrum (see screen) with Lucretius’ tāctilis, “that can be touched”. Andresian (p. 14) sets tangere beside quadrum for working a phone’s screen. In the house most screens are touchscreens, and plain quadrum is enough.

tactile.html: From tāctus, which is long by Lachmann’s law; its derivatives keep the long vowel, as āctiō and lēctiō do.

sources: Lewis & Short: quadrum · Lewis & Short: tactilis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 262.
